title: Current Liabilities & Accruals
description: Understand short-term obligations, accrued liabilities and common payable accounts.
html:
What is a current liability?

A current liability is an obligation generally expected to be settled within the entity's normal operating cycle or within the applicable short-term classification period.

Common examples

  • Accounts Payable
  • Wages Payable
  • Interest Payable
  • Taxes Payable
  • Current portions of certain long-term obligations

Accounts Payable

Accounts Payable usually arises when a company purchases goods or services on credit.

Example

A company purchases $8,000 of supplies on account.

Accrued liabilities

An accrued liability exists when an expense has been incurred but has not yet been paid.

Accrued wages

Employees have earned $5,000 by year-end, but payment will occur next period.

Account
Debit
Credit
Wages Expense
$5,000

Accrued interest

Interest can also accumulate before the company actually pays the lender.

Interest = Principal × Annual Rate × Time

A company has a $60,000 note at 8%. Three months of interest have accrued.

$60,000 × 8% × 3/12 = $1,200

Core idea

Accrual accounting recognizes obligations when they arise, not merely when cash is eventually paid.

quiz.prompt: A company owes employees $7,500 for work performed before year-end but will pay them next year. Which liability should be recognized?
quiz.explanation: The employees have already earned the wages, so the company recognizes Wages Expense and Wages Payable.
